beginner.summary: For developers and testers who know one programming language and basic HTTP and are new to SOAP. Covers the SOAP 1.1 and 1.2 message model, XML namespaces and XSD, faults, WSDL structure and binding styles, calling services with curl, Postman and SoapUI, mocks, generating and writing Java clients and services with Jakarta XML Web Services and Apache CXF, a .NET client with dotnet-svcutil, a first CoreWCF service, basic transport security and troubleshooting, ending with a tested order lookup service.
prerequisites: Programs in Java or C# at a basic level and can build a project with Maven or the dotnet CLI
Understands HTTP methods, headers and status codes
Has a laptop that can run a JDK 17 or later, the .NET SDK, Docker and SoapUI
outcomes: Read and hand-write SOAP 1.1 and 1.2 messages and interpret faults
Read a WSDL and XSD and trace an operation through the contract
Build, call and test a simple SOAP service in Java and .NET
Diagnose common SOAP failures with curl, SoapUI and a TCP monitor

intermediate.summary: For developers who have called or built a SOAP service and now design contracts and secure them. advanced.summary: For architects, senior engineers and platform owners who run SOAP estates. Covers gateway routing and policies, XML threat protection, WS-Security attack defence, SAML and WS-Trust federation, WS-Policy, reliability and idempotency, performance and load testing, observability, contract versioning, resilient clients, Kubernetes deployment, SOAP over JMS, SOAP-to-REST modernisation with strangler routing, OpenAPI mapping, REST facades, estate governance, advanced troubleshooting and a full modernisation capstone.
prerequisites: Has delivered at least one secured SOAP service or completed the intermediate level
Knows Kubernetes, an API gateway or a reverse proxy at a working level
Can read logs, metrics and traces and run load tests
outcomes: Harden SOAP endpoints against XML and WS-Security attacks
Operate SOAP services with measured performance, resilience and observability
Plan and execute a strangler migration from SOAP to REST with evidence
Govern, version and retire services in a mixed SOAP and REST estate
